intro:
A status message: something the reader needs to know about the screen they are on.

`Alert.Indicator` resolves both the icon and its colour from the alert's variant, so neither is passed in and both follow the active theme.

Use it for a condition that persists on the page. For something transient that arrives and leaves, use [Toast](/docs/components/toast).
usage:
<Alert variant="success">
  <Alert.Indicator />
  <Alert.Content>
    <Alert.Title>Payment received</Alert.Title>
    <Alert.Description>Your invoice has been paid.</Alert.Description>
  </Alert.Content>
</Alert>

parts.Indicator: Leading status icon, picked from the variant. Pass children to override it.
parts.Content: Flex-1 wrapper for the title and description.
parts.Title: Heading, coloured by the variant.

notes: Omit `Alert.Indicator` for a text-only alert. The legacy `icon` prop still renders, but prefer the indicator.

examples.title: With a title and description
examples.description: The indicator picks its icon from the variant, so most alerts need no `icon` prop.
examples.code:
<Alert variant="warning">
  <Alert.Indicator />
  <Alert.Content>
    <Alert.Title>Card expiring</Alert.Title>
    <Alert.Description>
      Your card ending 4242 expires next month.
    </Alert.Description>
  </Alert.Content>
</Alert>

examples.title: Title only
examples.description: Drop the description when the title says everything.

examples.title: A custom icon
examples.description: Pass `icon` on the root to replace the variant icon everywhere, or give `Alert.Indicator` children to replace it for one alert.
examples.code:
<Alert variant="info" icon={<ShieldCheckIcon size={18} />}>
  <Alert.Indicator />
  <Alert.Content>
    <Alert.Title>Two-factor authentication is on</Alert.Title>
  </Alert.Content>
</Alert>

examples.title: No icon
examples.description: Leave out `Alert.Indicator` for a text-only alert.
examples.code:
<Alert>
  <Alert.Content>
    <Alert.Title>Plain alert</Alert.Title>
    <Alert.Description>Omit Alert.Indicator for a text-only alert.</Alert.Description>
  </Alert.Content>
</Alert>
